format.description: The version of this file format. Always 1.

id.description: A name for this character, like "hero". It matches the file name.

body.description: "dynamic" moves and falls; "fixed" stays where it is put.

w.description: How wide the character is, in tiles.

h.description: How tall the character is, in tiles.

size.description: The size of the character, in tiles.

color.description: The colour it is drawn in, as # and six digits, like #e4572e.

upright.description: True if the character stays on its feet and cannot be tipped over. Left out means false.

kind.description: What this is to the game's rules and to behaviour files, like "crate", "spark" or "door".

figure.description: The figure it is drawn from, by id, like "hero". Left out means the coloured box.

id.description: A name for this clip, used once in this character, like "run".

poses.description: The poses of the character's figure it shows, in order, by id, like ["run-1", "run-2"].

fps.description: How many pictures a second it shows, from 1 to 60.

loop.description: True to go round again at the end, false to hold the last picture.

clips.description: The ways it moves, as runs of its figure's poses. "idle", "run", "jump", "fall" and "land" play by how it moves, and "air-jump", "wall" and "dash" by how a hero with "moves" moves; any other, like "push" or "talk", plays when the game or a cutscene asks. Left out means the first pose.

behaviour.description: The behaviour file that decides what it does, by id, like "critter".

tuning.description: The tuning file whose numbers decide how it moves, by id, like "hero".

touch.description: "sense": things pass through it and the game is told when one touches it, like a door. "take": the same, and it is taken away when a hero touches it, like a spark.

tuning.description: The tuning file with the hero's numbers and controls, by id, like "hero-moves".

double-jump.description: True to let the hero jump once more in the air. Left out means false.

wall-jump.description: True to let the hero slide down a wall and jump off it. Left out means false.

dash.description: True to let the hero dash. Left out means false.

moves.description: Set on the hero only: the framework walks and jumps it from a tuning file, with no game code. Walk and jump are always on; "double-jump", "wall-jump" and "dash" are each switched on here.

id.description: A name for this value, used once in this character, like "opens".

name.description: What an editor calls this value, in your own words, like "Opens". It is not translated.

about.description: A short help line for whoever sets this value. Left out means none.

shown.description: How the level view draws it: "tag" a small badge, "reach" a ring, "arrow" a line to another thing, "path" a line through places, "none" not at all. A number may be a tag, a reach or none; a switch, choice, words or leads-to value a tag or none; a thing an arrow or none; a path a path or none. Left out means the usual one for its type.

step.description: It moves in jumps of this size from "least". Left out means any number in between.

default.description: What a thing holds when it says nothing. Between "least" and "most".

default.description: The option a thing holds when it says nothing, by its name.

type.description: "thing": a link to other things in the same level.

kinds.description: The kinds of thing it may link to, like ["gate"]. Left out means any.

most.description: How many things it may link to, from 1 to 16. 1, or left out, means one thing, written as its id; more means a list of up to that many.

needed.description: True when every thing of this character must say it. Left out means false.

type.description: "path": a list of places in the level, one after another.

least.description: The fewest places it needs. Left out means 2.

most.description: The most places it may have. Left out means 64.

loop.description: True when the end of the path joins its start. Left out means false.

type.description: "leads-to": a way into another level, and a thing in it to come out beside.

needed.description: True when every thing of this character must say it. Left out means false.

values.description: The values its things may hold, like a number, a switch, a link to other things, a path or a way into another level. A thing in a level gives them. Left out means none.

opens.description: The "thing" value that lists what this switch opens, like "opens".

stays.description: The "switch" value that says this one stays down once pressed, like "stays". Left out means it comes up when nothing stands on it.

switch.description: Set on a plate or a button: it is pressed by what touches it, so it needs "touch": "sense". "opens" names the "thing" value that lists what it opens; "stays" names a "switch" value that makes it stay down once pressed.

opens.description: "walk-through": things pass through this character while it is open, like a gate. A fixed character with no "touch".

one-per-level.description: True when a level may hold only one thing of this character, like a goal. Left out means false.
